sections.h2: Who bills and collects property tax
sections.html:
Two offices in the Rogersville courthouse annex split the work. The Property Assessor decides the value. The Trustee takes that value and the commission's rate, makes the bill and collects it. Tax bills usually go out after the County Commission sets the rate and passes the budget, normally no later than October 15.

The Trustee's office is at 110 East Main Street, Room 203, Rogersville, TN 37857, phone (423) 272-7022. The Assessor is at 110 East Main Street, Room 201, phone (423) 272-8505. Weekday hours for both are eight to four, though the Trustee closes for lunch between noon and one.

sections.h2: Due dates, late interest and payment options
sections.html:
No interest is charged on payments made October 1 through the end of February. From March 1, any open balance picks up 1.5% a month.

The Trustee accepts partial payments, but the owner must sign a form each tax year before the first partial payment is taken. Cash, check, money order and debit or credit cards (Mastercard or Visa) are accepted. A card payment carries a 2.65% processing fee plus a $1.00 convenience fee. A satellite office at 150 South Central in Church Hill, phone (423) 357-4350, opens for the season from mid-October to mid-March. The county home page also links an online payment portal for property taxes.

sections.h2: How a Hawkins County tax bill is figured
sections.html:
Three steps make a bill: the assessor provides the assessed value, the commission sets the rate, and the Trustee multiplies them. The Trustee's page includes a tax calculator if you want to test a figure before the bills arrive.

The commission has 14 members, two from each of seven civil districts, and it adopts the rate along with the annual budget for the general, school and highway funds. A higher rate is a public decision with notices and hearings, so the commission's budget meetings before bills go out are the time to speak.

Start with the Assessor's office at (423) 272-8505 and ask for an informal review. Show why the value is too high, with sales of comparable homes or an appraisal. When the review fails, the next stops are the county Board of Equalization and then the State Board of Equalization. The assessor's page warns that deadlines are strictly enforced.

The county board hears cases in June each year. Assessment change notices go out in May, so watch your mail in spring, since a notice is sent only when a value changed.

  • A reappraisal updates values to current sales, and Tennessee Code 67-5-1601 requires the cycle.
  • After a reappraisal, the State Board of Equalization certifies a tax rate meant to bring in the same revenue as the year before, apart from new construction.
  • If the County Commission adopts a higher rate than the certified one, that counts as a tax increase and needs public notice and hearings.

Gather your evidence before you call: recent sale prices of similar homes nearby, photos of defects, and any appraisal you already have. The more specific the dollar figure you propose, the easier it is for the assessor or the board to act on it.

Tennessee offers relief to elderly and disabled homeowners and disabled military service members. Applications go to the Hawkins County Trustee. Income counts, and proof of income is required. The application must be completed no later than April 4 after the February 28 payment deadline.

Relief is a reimbursement from the state toward taxes already owed, not an exemption. You still receive a bill and must pay it. Relief covers only your primary residence, and the amount changes with your assessment and tax rate. The statutes are Tenn. Code Ann. 67-5-701 through 67-5-704.

Farm and forest owners can ask about greenbelt. Apply by March 15. If land later stops qualifying, a roll-back tax equal to three years of savings comes due.

Because the program pays you back after the bill is settled, do not skip or delay your payment while you wait for approval. Keep your receipt, since it supports the application.

A tax debt follows the parcel, which means the title company must get a payoff from the Trustee ahead of closing. Request a figure good through the expected closing date, with interest after March 1 included.

Taxes that stay unpaid are collected through the Hawkins County Chancery Court. The Clerk and Master, at 100 E. Main Street, Suite 316, Rogersville, collects delinquent property tax for the county and the towns. The number for delinquent tax questions is (423) 272-8150. The office keeps a delinquent tax sale list and offers online delinquent tax payments, searchable by parcel number.

Behind on taxes? Phone the Clerk and Master to learn whether your parcel is on the list.

A short routine keeps a Hawkins County sale on track. Call the Trustee at (423) 272-7022 for a payoff through your expected closing date. Call the Assessor at (423) 272-8505 to confirm the owner name and parcel details. If a past-due balance exists, ask the Clerk and Master whether the parcel has reached the delinquent list. Give the title company the payoff figure so it can pay the Trustee out of your proceeds at closing. A cash buyer can often close quickly enough to clear the balance before more interest builds.

sections.h2: Hawkins County for homeowners and sellers
sections.html:
Hawkins County covers about 500 square miles in the northeast corner of Tennessee, with Rogersville as the county seat. Church Hill is the largest city. Bulls Gap, Mount Carmel and Surgoinsville are towns, and Bean Station and Kingsport reach into the county.

There are 59,559 residents and about 28,006 housing units. Roughly 80.1% of homes are owner-occupied, valued at a median $176,300. Gross rent has a median of $785, household income $56,936, and monthly owner costs with a mortgage $1,136.

  • The county government does not issue building permits and has no zoning restrictions or code enforcement. Permits come through the State of Tennessee.
  • Septic records, if you need them for a sale, come from the Tennessee Department of Environment and Conservation. You may need the name of the original owner.
  • New 911 address questions go to (423) 272-7532.
  • School districts serving the county are Hawkins County, Kingsport City and Rogersville City, which covers elementary grades only.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Hawkins County property taxes?
faqs.a: Pay the Hawkins County Trustee at 110 East Main Street, Room 203, Rogersville, or at the Church Hill office from mid-October to mid-March. Online payment is linked from the county home page. Card payments add a 2.65% fee plus $1.00.

faqs.q: When do Hawkins County property taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: Delinquency begins once February ends. Interest of 1.5% per month is added from March 1. The Trustee accepts partial payments if the owner signs the required form for that tax year.

faqs.q: How do I reach the Hawkins County Property Assessor?
faqs.a: The office is at 110 East Main Street, Room 201, Rogersville, and the phone number is (423) 272-8505. It opens at eight and closes at four on weekdays.

faqs.q: When can I appeal a Hawkins County assessment?
faqs.a: The county Board of Equalization meets each June, after change notices go out in May. The assessor's office handles informal reviews first.

faqs.q: Who handles delinquent tax sales in Hawkins County?
faqs.a: The Chancery Court Clerk and Master handles them. Call (423) 272-8150 for delinquent tax questions. The office keeps a delinquent tax sale list.
